wave_evidence.claim: python -m scripts.code_map build --root . takes 2.9 seconds and is deterministic.
wave_evidence.observed: Build-only baseline held (~2.9s, gate 1). Full mechanism including worktree materialization measured at 3.25-3.77s across independent timing runs (gate 1 implementer, gate 3 case 8) -- a few hundred ms to under a second of overhead on top of the build, well within what a pre-commit hook can absorb.

wave_evidence.claim: A pre-commit hook that silently stages during a partial commit (git commit -p, git commit <path>) risks corrupting what the author intended to commit -- the Honest-Null Clause's named sharpest hazard.
wave_evidence.expected: The hazard needed active investigation, not presumption; a documented negative result was a legitimate outcome if it proved unclosable.
wave_evidence.observed: Hazard reproduced empirically by two independently-dispatched plan candidates, closed by an index-snapshot mechanism (build from git write-tree/commit-tree/worktree-add, never the live working tree), and proven closed at three tiers: unit (tests/test_code_map_precommit.py's PartialCommitTests), library-level (gate 3's cross-check), and real end-to-end (tests/test_code_map_precommit_e2e.py cases 4-5, independently reproduced by the g1/g3 reviewers by hand, not merely trusted). No honest-null triggered -- the mechanism holds.
wave_evidence.source: PLAN_ALTERNATIVES.md; PLAN_CRITIC.md findings 4-5 and their disposition; tests/test_code_map_precommit_e2e.py::PathspecRestrictedPartialCommitTests, ::HunkRestrictedPartialCommitTests

wave_evidence.claim: This repo's own dev checkout is a linked worktree sharing one .git/hooks with sibling worktrees, so a hook installed from one lane governs commits made from every other lane -- a cold plan critic's named blocking finding.
wave_evidence.expected: The mechanism needed to resolve the shared hooks directory correctly (never a hardcoded .git/hooks join) and be proven to fire from a second worktree it was never installed from.
wave_evidence.observed: resolve_git_hooks_dir (scripts/install_constellation.py) correctly resolves the shared hooks dir via git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path hooks, verified against this actual checkout's real layout (git worktree list showed 8-12 sibling worktrees across the run). Case 7 of the e2e suite installs from one worktree and commits for real from a second sharing the same .git; the hook fires there with no install step run in that second worktree. Independently reproduced by hand by the g3 reviewer.

wave_evidence.claim: No timeout anywhere would mean fail-open covers a crash but not a hang, which blocks a commit exactly as hard as an uncaught crash -- a cold plan critic's named blocking finding.
wave_evidence.expected: Every subprocess call in the mechanism needed an explicit timeout with fail-open coverage on TimeoutExpired.
wave_evidence.observed: Every git subprocess call in scripts/code_map/precommit.py funnels through one _run(runner, ...) helper with an explicit 10s timeout; a forced-timeout test (mocking a hang) confirms the shim still exits 0 within a bounded wall-clock window (~10-15s), independently re-run by the g1 reviewer.
